Account.description: An account: a node that holds assets. AccountType is what kind of account it is (brokerage, retirement plan, deposit, credit card, loan), with an extension table for the more specific type. It is held at InstitutionId, which knows it as ExternalAccountId (the account's identifier there, which orders sent to it carry). Currency (ISO 4217) is the currency the account is kept in: its transaction lines' amounts and its holdings' market values are in it, as its institution reports them. An account has no model of its own: it is in exactly one portfolio (its Edge), and follows the model that governs that portfolio.

Brokerage.description: A brokerage account: an account of type Brokerage, with its more specific type (taxable, or an IRA).

Event.description: The log: every input as it entered the ledger, never changed or deleted. EventType says what kind (a fixed code) and SchemaVersion which version of its payload; Payload is the kind's own fields, as JSON, read back by kind and version. Holdings, orders' states and every other derived state are folded from these. Every event that changes holdings is complete in itself: an exchange within the books balances. RowVersion (each row written takes the next number) orders the log. TransactionId is the transaction it came in: one or more events committed or refused as a unit, supplied by the client; a transaction's events are contiguous in the log. The source supplies EventId (for a broker's messages, a name-based ID from the source and its own IDs) and (Source, SourceId) is idempotent, so a replayed message is recorded once. CorrelationId is what it belongs to (an order: the first of its replace chain); CausationId what caused it.

Institution.description: An institution that holds accounts: a broker, a bank, a card issuer. Source is the connection the system reaches it through (Schwab's API, the aggregator, the simulator): for a broker, which adapter its orders go to. What is particular to one account (its identifier there) is on the account.

Alert.description: A compliance violation found by the rules: one per node and rule, removed when the rule is satisfied again.

Asset.description: Anything that can be held: cash, a stock, a fund, a bond, an option, a future or a coin. Its identity is a node, its Symbol rows are its names in each scheme (Currency, Ticker, Cusip), and one extension table by asset type holds what is particular to it. Its price is quoted in QuoteCurrency (ISO 4217; a currency is quoted in itself, at 1). Market value in an account's currency is quantity × QuantityFactor × price × PriceFactor × the price of QuoteCurrency in the account's currency: QuantityFactor is the units one quantity stands for (100 shares for an option, a futures contract's multiplier), PriceFactor the units a quoted price stands for (0.01 for a bond priced per 100 of face value, or a future quoted in cents).

Cash.description: An asset of type Cash: a currency, held in units of itself at a price of one.

Crypto.description: An asset of type Crypto: a coin or token on a blockchain.

Edge.description: A link in the household's tree: ChildNodeId is in ParentNodeId. Keyed on the child alone, so every node has at most one parent. The household is the root and holds only portfolios; a portfolio holds portfolios and accounts. Position orders a parent's children (the household's order, the same on every device). Since is the market day the child has been in this parent, from that day's close: a move between portfolios is dated, and is also recorded in the log as a NodeMoved event, so a portfolio's history is never rewritten.

Equity.description: An asset of type Equity: a share in a company.

FixedIncome.description: An asset of type Fixed Income: a bond or note. Quantity is face value; price is per 100 of face value.

Fund.description: An asset of type Fund: a share in a pooled vehicle (an exchange-traded fund, a mutual fund, a money market fund).

Future.description: An asset of type Future: an agreement to buy or sell its underlying at a set price on its expiration date.

Node.description: Anything in the tenant with a name: the household, a portfolio, an account, a person or an asset (NodeType), and whether it is active or closed (NodeStatus). A closed node keeps its history and is hidden; it is never deleted once it has history.

Option.description: An asset of type Option: the right to buy (call) or sell (put) its underlying asset at the strike price until it expires.

Price.description: The latest price of a symbol in a currency: the price of one unit of what the symbol names, as quoted, in units of Currency (NVDA in USD; USD in USD, which is 1; USD in GBP). Published by the market data feed and, for constants such as a currency's price in itself, from the server's initial prices at startup. Ticks are ephemeral: never persisted, synced, or served by the API.

ClosingPrice.description: A symbol's official closing price on a market day, in a currency, as traded that day (not adjusted for later splits or dividends). Loaded from the market data vendor for the days the tenant's history needs, and each market day after the close; the paper broker fills market orders at it, and the rules value accounts at it. Ephemeral: reloaded at startup, never persisted.

Dividend.description: A cash dividend: Amount per share, in Currency, to whoever held the shares at the close before ExDate, paid on PaymentDate. From the market data vendor; the rules credit it to paper accounts. Ephemeral.

InterestRate.description: An interest rate published for a day, as a fraction a year (0.0405 for 4.05%): the risk-free rate is Code TBILL-13W, the 13-week Treasury bill's coupon equivalent (its investment yield), from the Treasury's daily bill rates. Ephemeral.

Split.description: A stock split effective at the open of Date: each share held at the close before becomes Ratio shares (2 for a 2-for-1 split, 0.1 for a 1-for-10 reverse split). From the market data vendor; the rules apply it to paper accounts. Ephemeral.

Model.description: A model: a complete recipe for a portfolio, what to hold (ModelKind, with an extension table per kind) and how much of it (the cash rule). Fixed weights are its Weight rows; an index model's are its IndexModel row; a custom list's its CustomListModel and CustomListMember rows. CashRule None is fully invested; FixedAmount keeps CashAmount in cash; VolatilityTarget sets cash each day so the whole portfolio's volatility, measured over VolatilityWindow market days, stays within VolatilityBand of VolatilityTarget. Band is the smallest trade worth making, as a fraction of the book's value. Targets are whole shares, rounded down. Many portfolios may share one model, and so share its risk.

Weight.description: One asset's weight in a fixed-weights model: its fraction of the book's value (0.25 for a quarter). What the weights don't add up to stays in cash.

Position.description: A holding: what an account's events add up to for one asset, derived by the rules after every change. Ephemeral and written only by the server: rebuilt from the events at startup, read through the API and client sync, never in the database. Its market value is Quantity × QuantityFactor × the asset's effective price × PriceFactor × the rate from QuoteCurrency to AccountCurrency.

EffectivePrice.description: The price the rules use for an asset, as quoted, in its quote currency: the market's latest, or else the last purchase or sale. Derived by the rules; ephemeral, written only by the server.

CurrencyRate.description: The price of one unit of a currency in another (1 for a currency in itself). Derived by the rules; ephemeral, written only by the server.

AccountFlow.description: An account's net contributions: its deposits less its withdrawals. Derived by the rules; ephemeral, written only by the server.

AccountDay.description: An account at one market day's close: its value, the day's deposits and withdrawals, its time-weighted return and the risk-free rate's. Derived by the rules; ephemeral, written only by the server.

AccountStatistic.description: An account's performance measured from its daily returns: total and annualized return, volatility, Sharpe ratio and worst drawdown; ranked after 20 returns. Derived by the rules; ephemeral, written only by the server.

JobRun.description: One run of a job for this tenant: the log of what ran, when, why and how it ended. A run by hand is asked for by inserting a row with Status Requested (the caller supplies the key and RequestedTime); the scheduler takes it up after the commit, and refuses it if the job is unknown, a service, off (every schedule of it Off) or already running. The server records scheduled runs, a service's starts and stops, and every outcome. A run still Requested or Running when the server starts is marked Interrupted: what it did is not confirmed. JobScheduleId is the schedule that started it (no reference: a schedule can be deleted, its runs stay).

JobSchedule.description: A job of this tenant's, and when it runs: Job is the job's key (the [Job] attribute on its class, such as GenerateOrders). Status is what is asked for: Off (it doesn't run on its own), On (a service runs now, until changed; not for a task) or Scheduled. Scheduled, a task runs at each CronSchedule time; a service is on from each CronSchedule time to the next StopSchedule time. Both are Quartz cron expressions, read in TimeZone (IANA). A job marked for market days skips the NYSE's holidays. A missed run is skipped, not made up. The scheduler acts on each commit: a change takes effect at once; turning a row Off or deleting it stops what it started, cancelling a run in progress.

Portfolio.description: A portfolio: a node that holds portfolios and accounts (through Edge) and keeps its own statistics. ModelId is its model: a value governs every account beneath it, except those beneath a lower portfolio with a model of its own; null inherits its parent's (a top-level portfolio without one is tracked, not managed). Its restricted list is its Restriction rows, added to its parents'.

Restriction.description: A company a portfolio won't hold, by symbol (a ticker, say). Restrictions accumulate down the tree: a portfolio excludes its own and every parent's.

IndexModel.description: An index model (ModelKind ConstantWeightIndex or IndexWeightIndex): the Companies largest US companies by full market value under the published rules of the index IndexCode names (TA500), less the portfolio's restrictions, weighted by market value at each quarterly rebalance. Constant Weight trades back to those weights every day; Index Weight holds the quantities until the next rebalance. Its weights are derived each day from the ranking data, never saved.

CustomListModel.description: A custom list model (ModelKind CustomList): the companies the customer names (its CustomListMember rows), weighted equally, by market value, or by the fractions he gives (ListWeighting), and traded back to those weights every day (IsConstantWeight) or only when the list or the weights change.

CustomListMember.description: A company on a custom list, by symbol; Fraction is its weight when the list is weighted by the customer's fractions, and empty otherwise.

PortfolioDay.description: A portfolio at one market day's close: the combined value of the accounts beneath it that day, the day's flows (theirs, plus an account's value when it joins and less it when it leaves), its time-weighted return and the risk-free rate's. Rough for now: the first piece of the mini-accounting system. Derived by the rules; ephemeral, written only by the server.

PortfolioStatistic.description: A portfolio's performance measured from its daily returns, as an account's is: total and annualized return, volatility, Sharpe ratio and worst drawdown; ranked after 20 returns. Derived by the rules; ephemeral, written only by the server.
